name: Venom-Thurible
specific_features: Fumaroles that release visible green-tinted toxic gas plumes
Mineral springs that deposit colorful but lethal arsenic crystal formations
description: Venom-Thurible is a volcanic world where the geological chemistry has produced an environment toxic beyond the already harsh baseline of its class. The fumarole fields release plumes of arsenic-laden gas that are visible as green-tinted columns rising from the surface, their color a literal warning of the lethal chemistry they carry. The planet's surface is stained in improbable colors by the exotic mineral deposits, arsenic crystals forming vivid yellow and green formations around spring vents while bismuth compounds produce rainbow-sheened deposits that would be beautiful if they were not actively dangerous to every form of known life.

The toxic atmosphere combines the standard volcanic cocktail of sulfur compounds with arsenic vapor, antimony dust, and traces of hydrogen cyanide produced by volcanic reactions with nitrogen compounds in the crust. The resulting atmosphere is among the most lethally hostile ever documented, requiring not merely sealed suits but specialized chemical-resistant environmental gear that must be inspected after every surface excursion for microperforations that could allow penetration of the arsenic-laden air. The heat compounds the danger, the elevated temperatures increasing the volatility of compounds that would be merely hazardous on a cooler world.

The mineral deposits on Venom-Thurible are the product of a geological history that concentrated toxic elements in the upper crust to an unusual degree, the planet's formation occurring in a region of space enriched in heavy metalloids by a nearby supernova remnant. The volcanic recycling of this enriched crust has produced surface concentrations of arsenic, antimony, and bismuth that exceed any other known world by orders of magnitude. The acid rain that falls during eruption events dissolves and redeposits these minerals in ever-more-concentrated formations, the planet essentially refining its own toxic chemistry with each geological cycle.

The arsenic and antimony deposits are commercially valuable for semiconductor manufacturing and specialized metallurgy, but extraction requires equipment and protocols that drive costs to the edge of viability. Bismuth, used in medical and industrial applications, is present in grades that make Venom-Thurible a primary supplier despite the operational challenges. All surface work is conducted by remotely operated systems where possible, the human crews remaining in sealed orbital facilities and descending to the surface only when remote systems cannot accomplish the task. The green plumes rise from the fumaroles in their perpetual toxic offering, a censer burning poison instead of incense for a congregation of machines.
